name: Zonal Method (Bhate and Tokuta)
definition: An extension to the zonal method dealing with effects between surfaces and volumes. It eliminates the assumption of medium isotropy by representing phase function and radiance using spherical harmonics, while surfaces remain ideal diffuse.
summary: The Zonal Method extends classical global illumination by using spherical harmonics for anisotropic scattering and an extended hemicube to compute form factors for volume-surface interactions.
